prerequisites: The student should have passed the 1st year course, Graphic Expression and Computer-Aided Design (6 ECTS) and the 2nd year course, Industrial Drawing (6 ECTS).

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire knowledge and abilities to develop, organize and manage projects.
Know the organizational structure and functions of a project office.

Ability for the drafting, signing and development of projects in the field of industrial engineering, whose objective is, in accordance with the knowledge acquired as established in section 5 of Order CIN/351/2009 of February 9, the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or exploitation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Ability for the direction of the activities subject to the engineering projects described in skill HA_21.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and aptitudes in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to organize and plan within the company, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Teamwork: Actively collaborate with a group of people to achieve a common goal by combining different talents.
Understands the interrelationships between all agents related to the project.
Interprets the fundamental concepts and norms related to industrial projects.
Understands the aspects and characteristics involved in the technical studies of industrial activity.
Performs and carries out the definition, design, planning, development and monitoring of a project.
Interprets and prepares the specific technical documentation of a project in their specialty.

syllabus_topics: 1.1. INTRODUCTION TO PROJECT DIRECTION AND MANAGEMENT
T.2.- GENERAL CRITERIA FOR PROJECT DEVELOPMENT
2.3. TECHNICAL PROJECTS IN THE FIELD OF MECHANICS
T.3.- NORMATIVE APPLICATION IN THE DESIGN OF MECHANICAL PROJECTS.
3.1.- COMPETENCIES OF THE GRADUATE - INDUSTRIAL TECHNICAL ENGINEER.
3.2.- APPLICATION OF OFFICIAL REGULATIONS IN THE MECHANICAL FIELD.
4.1.- COMPETENCIES, AUTHORIZATION, LEGALIZATION AND COMMISSIONING OF INDUSTRIAL INSTALLATIONS.
4.2.- AGENTS INVOLVED IN THE LEGALIZATION OF INDUSTRIAL INSTALLATIONS.
4.3. CONTROL AND TECHNICAL DIRECTION OF PROJECTS.
T.5.- REGULATIONS ON REPRESENTATION OF DIAGRAMS AND PLANS IN ENGINEERING PROJECTS.
5.2.- TYPES OF PLANS USED IN MECHANICAL PROJECTS.
5.3.- PLANS REQUIRED DEPENDING ON THE TYPE OF PROJECT.
assessment_rules: The subject will be considered passed when both the theoretical exam grade and the project grade are equal to or greater than 5. The global evaluation test will consist of a theoretical exam (25%) and a project (75%). Students must be able to demonstrate authorship of works, practicals, and any type of evaluable activity; otherwise, the grade for those activities will be zero. Unauthorized use of materials or electronic devices during the evaluation test may lead to withdrawal from the exam and a grade of 0.
